title: Typed runlet parameter validation, dry-run mode, and RBAC gating for Private admin flows
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Enable a safer, more predictable execution surface for admin runlets used by support and SREs in Private/VPC deployments. Work includes: 1) a typed parameter schema for runlets with validation at submission and at execution time; 2) a dry-run execution mode that simulates side effects and produces canonical diffs and telemetry without mutating state; 3) an RBAC gating layer that enforces policy and emits auditable decisions; 4) Console telemetry hooks to surface dry-run vs live executions and per-step latencies. This removes a common class of accidental writes and gives first-line support the ability to rehearse flows in regulated environments.
acceptance_criteria: Runlet manifests support explicit parameter schemas (type, required, allowlist/denylist, min/max where applicable) and are stored in control plane
Submission API rejects requests that fail schema validation with clear error codes and suggestions
Dry-run mode executes validation + planner + simulation steps and emits a non- actionable mutation plan (diff) visible in Console and in run logs
RBAC gate evaluates the caller's role and policy for each non-dry execution, blocks when policy denies, and writes audit events to the private audit store
Telemetry shows dry-run vs live counts, per-step durations, and a dry-run success/failure rate dashboard; rollout behind feature flag
E2E tests cover schema validation, dry-run fidelity, RBAC decisioning, and audit log entries for Private deployments
progress: Week 1: schema design and API prototypes (completed). Week 2: control-plane validation + unit tests (done). Week 3: agent-side simulator prototype and dry-run planner (in progress). Week 4: RBAC hook integration and console telemetry dashboards (planned). Blocking: finalizing audit storage format with Security and Compliance.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Where to validate: we chose a hybrid approach. Fast reject at submission (control plane) to give immediate feedback to callers, plus a second defensive enforcement at the agent side to prevent drift when runlets are executed directly by private agents.

Dry-run fidelity: full fidelity simulation is expensive. We will implement a planner that computes expected mutations and a best-effort simulator for common action types (DB writes, service calls). For unknown/custom runlets we will fallback to a conservative simulated outcome and mark as 'partial-simulation'.

RBAC enforcement model: decision evaluated in control plane for hosted flows, but for Private/VPC we mirror policy bundles to the agent for offline decisioning. This trades complexity for availability in air-gapped environments.
implementation_notes: API shape: POST /runlets/execute with query param ?dry_run=true and a 'params' payload validated against stored JSON Schema-like manifest. We'll version manifests to allow safe rollouts. Agent runtime will expose a --simulate flag that returns a structured mutation plan. Audit events follow the existing audit-event schema and include field 'simulation': true/false.
tests_and_qa: Unit tests for schema validation, integration tests between control plane and agent simulator. Add two smoke scenarios to the runbook-evals harness: (1) idempotent safe flow (should pass dry-run and live), (2) destructive flow (dry-run must show diffs; live needs RBAC approval). Add a chaos test that replays simulated audit events into the audit-processor to ensure downstream tooling tolerates 'simulation' flag.
